Okra Stew

Served at: Yalda Night

Serves 6Prep 15 minCook 45 min

Okra Stew is a hearty and comforting dish traditionally served during Yalda Night, the Iranian celebration of the winter solstice. This stew combines tender okra with tomatoes and aromatic spices, symbolizing warmth and togetherness as families gather to welcome the longest night of the year.

Ingredients

  • 1 lb (450 g) fresh okra, trimmed
  • 2 tbsp olive oil
  • 1 large onion, finely chopped
  • 3 cloves garlic, minced
  • 2 cups (480 ml) crushed tomatoes
  • 1 cup (240 ml) vegetable or chicken broth
  • 1 tsp ground turmeric
  • 1 tsp ground cumin
  • 1/2 tsp ground cinnamon
  • Salt and pepper to taste
  • 1 tbsp lemon juice
  • Fresh parsley, chopped (for garnish)

Method

  1. Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat.
  2. Add chopped onion and sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes.
  3. Add minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant.
  4. Stir in turmeric, cumin, and cinnamon, cooking for 30 seconds to release their aroma.
  5. Add crushed tomatoes and broth, stirring to combine.
  6. Add the trimmed okra to the pot, stirring gently to coat with the sauce.
  7. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
  8. Bring the stew to a simmer, then reduce heat to low and cover.
  9. Cook for 30-35 minutes, stirring occasionally, until okra is tender and the stew has thickened.
  10. Stir in lemon juice and adjust seasoning if needed.
  11. Garnish with chopped fresh parsley before serving.

Tips

  • Use fresh okra for the best texture and flavor; frozen okra can be used but may alter the stew's consistency.
  • Serve the stew with saffron rice or warm flatbread to complete the Yalda Night meal.
  • For a richer stew, add a handful of cooked chickpeas or lamb pieces during the simmering stage.
